Dear Freedom of Information Officer:
Under the Connecticut Freedom of Information Act, Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-200 et seq., including § 1-210(a), I request copies of the public records described below held by the Town of New Haven, including its departments, boards, commissions, and offices.
In this request, "AI tools" means Microsoft Copilot (including Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, Copilot Studio, and GitHub Copilot), Google Gemini (including Gemini for Google Workspace and Gemini accessed through Google Cloud or Vertex AI), and Anthropic's Claude (including Claude.ai team or enterprise plans and the Claude API). This includes tools bought directly, through a reseller, under an enterprise or cooperative purchasing agreement, or bundled into another license.

1. Contracts and costs. All contracts, license or subscription agreements, terms of service accepted on the Town's behalf, quotes, purchase orders, invoices, amendments, renewals, and payment records for any AI tool. Also any budget line items, appropriations, or approvals by the Board of Selectmen, Town Council, Board of Finance, or similar body that relate to these purchases.
2. Number of accounts and licenses. Records showing the number of licenses or seats purchased and the number of active user accounts for each AI tool, broken out by department where such records exist. This includes license-assignment reports or exports from the Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, or Anthropic administrative consoles.
3. Token usage and usage-based cost. Records showing token consumption, API call volume, credits used, or other usage metrics for each AI tool, and the resulting usage-based charges. This includes monthly or periodic usage reports, billing statements, and billing-dashboard exports.
4. Policy on internal use. Any policy, guideline, memo, administrative directive, acceptable-use standard, procedure, or training material governing employees' use of AI tools for internal work, such as drafting documents, analyzing data, writing code, or summarizing meetings. Please include drafts under active consideration and records of their approval or adoption.
5. Policy on communication with residents. Any policy, guideline, memo, or procedure governing the use of AI tools in communications with residents or the public. This includes letters, emails, website or social media content, chatbots, responses to public inquiries, and any requirement to disclose or review AI-generated content.
6. Documented corrections on AI use. Records documenting instances in which an employee was counseled, warned, corrected, retrained, or disciplined about the use of AI tools. This includes emails, memos, incident or IT security reports, and notices of policy violations. I recognize that some of this material may fall under § 1-210(b)(2); I ask that the Town redact names and personally identifying details rather than withhold whole records, and that it provide any existing aggregate counts or summaries of such instances.

Time frame. Records dated from January 1, 2025 through the date the Town conducts its search.

Withheld material. If any record or part of a record is withheld, please cite the specific statutory exemption for each item and release all reasonably segregable, non-exempt portions.

I understand that § 1-206(a) calls for a response within four business days of receipt. If gathering the records will take longer, please acknowledge this request, provide an estimated completion date, and release records on a rolling basis as they become available.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Under the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. 552, I request copies of the following records:

1. User manuals, standard operating procedures, job aids, and training materials (including slide decks and course guides) for the Customer Profile Management System (CPMS), the CPMS Support Service (ESB2), and the National Appointment Scheduling System (NASS), created or in use from 1 January 2015 to the date of search.

2. The current "National Background, Identity, and Security Check Operating Procedures" (NaBISCOP), and every version or revision table issued after the version produced in Wagafe v. Biden, W.D. Wash. No. 2:17-cv-00094, Dkt. 665-22 (DEF-00431506), including any version issued in connection with the rescission of the Controlled Application Review and Resolution Program (CARRP).

3. The CARRP rescission notice or memorandum, and any replacement national security vetting policy, from 1 January 2026 to the date of search.

4. Standard operating procedures and guidance for biometrics collection at Application Support Centers (ASCs), including the ASC SOP(s) reviewed in the DHS Privacy Office's October 2017 CPMS/NASS Privacy Compliance Review and all later versions, and procedures for fingerprint waivers, biometric reuse, and identity verification.

5. Procedures, guidance, privacy threshold analyses, and agreements governing USCIS biometric or criminal history queries to foreign partner countries, from 1 January 2015 to the date of search, including:
   a. procedures for CPMS requests for background checks to a foreign partner country;
   b. USCIS use of the International Biometric Information Sharing program (DHS/ALL/PIA-095) – not the former Interagency Border Inspection System;
   c. the international arrangements cited in footnote 35 of the proposed rule "Collection and Use of Biometrics by U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services" (90 FR 49062, 3 November 2025; docket USCIS-2025-0205);
   d. records on the "automated data-sharing capabilities" to query foreign partner countries for criminal history record information described in that proposed rule.

The following records are already public and are excluded: the c. 2021 NaBISCOP and the December 2010 NaBISCOP excerpt; the CARRP and FDNS training exhibits filed in Wagafe (Dkts. 665 and 666); the 2011 FDNS SOP; and published DHS/USCIS PIAs (including 008(a), 048(a), 057, 060 series, and DHS/ALL/PIA-095) and the 2017 CPMS/NASS Privacy Compliance Review.

I am happy to receive records on a rolling basis and in electronic format, and to discuss narrowing the scope if needed.

I request a fee waiver, as disclosure is in the public interest: it will contribute significantly to public understanding of how USCIS conducts biometric and background checks and shares biometric data with foreign governments, and I have no commercial interest. If a waiver is denied, I agree to pay fees up to $25; please contact me before exceeding that.

Thank you,
Jordan Ellis

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jordan Ellis

title: Obama Presidential Library: August 2016 CIA Courier Briefing to Rice/NSC re: Putin

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I. Subject Matter and Scope

I request all executive, national security, and administrative records originating from or maintained by the Office of the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs (Susan Rice) and/or the National Security Council (NSC) Secretariat between July 15, 2016, and September 30, 2016, inclusive.

This request targets all records — regardless of physical form — concerning, referencing, or summarizing the sensitive intelligence material delivered via courier (the "Eyes Only" or "Top Secret Envelope") from the Central Intelligence Agency to the White House regarding Russian President Vladimir Putin's direct role in directing the 2016 U.S. election interference campaign, as first publicly reported by Greg Miller in The Washington Post ("Obama's secret struggle to punish Putin for election interference," June 23, 2017), including the internal deliberations that preceded the October 7, 2016 joint DHS/ODNI public attribution statement.

For guidance, here is the article where the existence of the envelope is mentioned: 
https://www.washingtonpost.com/graphics/2017/world/national-security/obama-putin-election-hacking/

The scope includes, but is not limited to:

1. Internal emails, text communications, and electronic messages sent to or received by Ambassador Susan Rice, Deputy National Security Advisor Ben Rhodes, Deputy National Security Advisor Avril Haines, Chief of Staff Denis McDonough, or NSC staff regarding this intelligence.

2. "Night notes," daily briefing materials, cover memos, executive summary sheets, and intelligence routing slips accompanying or summarizing the CIA briefing packet.

3. Official meeting summaries, readouts, attendee logs, action-item tracking logs, and personal notes generated during or immediately following NSC Principals Committee or Deputies Committee deliberations on this material.

4. Any drafts, talking points, or option papers prepared for the President regarding potential responses to the reported Russian activity during this period.

5. Photographs of the actual top secret envelope itself. Specifically, this is a request for any photographs of either the sealed or opened envelope delivered to the White House taken in order to confirm receipt. 

III. Concurrent Mandatory Declassification Review Request

To the extent any responsive records are withheld in whole or in part on the basis of classification under FOIA Exemption (b)(1) or the corresponding PRA restriction category, I request that those records be concurrently referred for Mandatory Declassification Review pursuant to Executive Order 13526, Section 3.5, so that this review may proceed in parallel rather than sequentially.

IV. Public Interest Fee Waiver

Disclosure is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of government operations and is not primarily in my commercial interest. The processing of intelligence on 2016 foreign election interference remains a matter of substantial, ongoing public interest involving national security governance, executive decision-making, and historical accountability, and the requested records would be made publicly available through MuckRock News.

V. Expedited Processing

I request expedited processing pursuant to 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(E) given the sustained public and media interest in this subject matter and my role as an active member of the news media disseminating FOIA-obtained records on this topic.

VI. Format and Processing

Please produce all responsive records in electronic format (PDF) via email or secure file transfer. If any portions are withheld under a statutory or PRA exemption, release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions. For any records withheld in full or in part, provide a Vaughn index itemizing each withheld record or redaction and the specific statutory or PRA basis claimed. If any records are referred to the Central Intelligence Agency or another agency for consultation under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6) or 44 U.S.C. § 2208, please notify me of the referral and the referred agency's identity.

Thank you for the work that the Obama Presidential Library does every day.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware
